title: passiflora cochinchinensis subsp. glaberrima
intro: Passiflora cochinchinensis subsp. glaberrima, commonly known as the Thai or Vietnamese passionflower, is a subspecies of the Passiflora cochinchinensis plant, a type of flowering vine native to Southeast Asia. This plant is valued for its potential health benefits, including its ability to reduce anxiety and insomnia, as well as alleviate symptoms of menopause and other conditions. The therapeutic actions of Passiflora cochinchinensis subsp. glaberrima are attributed to its sedative and anxiolytic effects, which are thought to be mediated by its bioactive constituents, including flavonoids, alkaloids, and lignans. The bioactive constituents of this plant, such as flavokawains and isovitexin, have been shown to possess antioxidant, anti-inflammatory, and neuroprotective properties.
